name: coding-auth-token-refresh
description: Coding session. The scripted title is too long and must be cut to 8 words.

chunk.speaker: Pratham
chunk.text: the dashboard keeps logging people out after about an hour. I think it's the token refresh. can you look at apps/web/lib/auth/refresh.ts

I read refresh.ts. Two tabs can call refreshSession() at the same time. The first call rotates the refresh token, so the second call sends a token that is already revoked and the API answers 401 invalid_grant. That 401 is what triggers the logout.

chunk.speaker: Pratham
chunk.text: yes that matches, it only happens to people with multiple tabs open. what's the fix

Two options: (a) a BroadcastChannel lock so only one tab refreshes and the others wait for the new token, or (b) have the server accept the previous refresh token for a short grace window. (a) needs no backend change.

chunk.speaker: Pratham
chunk.text: let's do both. go with the BroadcastChannel lock now, and I'll ask Ojas to add a 10 second grace window on the server by Friday. also access tokens stay at 1 hour, we're not changing that
Done. Added a lock in refresh.ts using BroadcastChannel('auth-refresh'); tabs that lose the lock wait up to 5 seconds for the new token. Tests pass: npm test -- refresh (14 passed).

chunk.speaker: Pratham
chunk.text: nice. one thing I don't know - does Safari private mode even support BroadcastChannel? we should check
I am not certain. I'd verify it in Safari before relying on it.

mock_replies.title: Fixing the dashboard logout bug caused by a refresh token race between browser tabs
mock_replies.summary: Pratham and the assistant traced hourly dashboard logouts to two tabs refreshing the session at once, which sent a revoked refresh token and returned 401. A BroadcastChannel lock was added in refresh.ts and tests pass. Pratham will ask Ojas for a 10 second server-side grace window by 2026-09-18; access tokens stay at 1 hour.
